name: profile-close-window-light
prompt: Vertical 9:16 close-up portrait, photographed on an 85mm lens at f/1.8. One masked figure fills the lower two thirds of the frame, seen in three-quarter view from the wearer's left side, chin lifted and head tipped back as if staring up at something enormous overhead. The head is covered completely by a charcoal grey hand-knitted balaclava of chunky ribbed wool with no openings at all: no eye holes, no mouth hole, a smooth blank knitted face. A bold white yarn ring is stitched in a circle around the whole face, and high inside that ring, over the wearer's left eye on the side nearest the camera, sits a small red felt triangle with softly rounded corners, set off-centre toward the upper edge of the ring rather than in the middle of the face. The balaclava tucks down into the raised corduroy collar of a modern olive waxed cotton jacket, and one hand in a black knitted glove rests on that collar, the jacket cuff pulled down over the wrist so no skin shows anywhere. Low late-afternoon sun comes through an unseen window from the side, raking across the knit so every loop and fibre of the wool catches warm amber light and casts tiny shadows, while the far side of the head falls into soft shade. Behind and above the figure, soft and blurred, rises a towering wall of stacked paper reams and bundled documents in cool off-white and pale grey, filling the upper part of the picture; on the edge of one sheet near the figure's sightline, the printed heading "THE RULES" in plain black capital letters is just readable through the blur. Warm amber light on the wool against cool paper white behind, fine film grain, natural contemporary British interior, a still photograph of cloth, wool and paper only.
